intro: Lesson 18. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَيْلٌۭ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ (١) ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ٱكْتَالُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ (٢) وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَو وَّزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ (٣) أَلَا يَظُنُّ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَنَّهُم مَّبْعُوثُونَ (٤) لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍۢ (٥) يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلنَّاسُ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ (٦)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Woe to those who give less [than due],
Who, when they take a measure from people, take in full.
But if they give by measure or by weight to them, they cause loss.
Do they not think that they will be resurrected
The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds?

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Idgham without ghunnah: tanween into ل; heavy ط
Merge, no hum; full mouth on ط
Tongue covers the roof of the mouth

keywords.def: those who give less than due

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Mutaffifin 83:1-6 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 83:1-6 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 83:1-6 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: On the pupil PDF, circle the heavy letters in 83:1 to 6.
questions.a: ط in لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ; خ in يُخْسِرُونَ; ظ in يَظُنُّ and عَظِيمٍ; ق in يَقُومُ.

questions.q: Give a modern example of 'giving less than due' that is not about weighing food.
questions.a: For example: doing less work than you are paid for, or selling broken goods as new.

options: take in full but give less
questions.a: A) take in full but give less. 83:2 to 3: they take in full from people but cause loss when they measure or weigh for others.

questions.q: Al-Mutaffifin 83:6: «يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: A shopkeeper gives you a little less than you paid for, and nobody notices. Why is this so serious that a surah begins with 'Woe'?
questions.a: It is stealing and cheating; Allah sees it, and every person will stand before Him (83:4 to 6).
